metadata.note: Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit (SMART), the commuter railroad that restored passenger trains to the old Northwestern Pacific corridor in Sonoma and Marin counties, California, 46 years after the NWP's last trains south of Willits. Three features with nested geometry, one per extent of the line: Sonoma County Airport - San Rafael (25 Aug 2017), Larkspur extension (14 Dec 2019), Windsor extension (31 May 2025). One company throughout, so no Rule 4 split.
not_yet_sourced: Actual 2017-2024 weekday timetables (headways for those years are derived from round-trip counts or assumed from the 2026 feed).
Opening date of Petaluma North station (open in the 2026 GTFS; not separately dated here).
Exact COVID-era dates: the 2020 cut and the May 2021 increase are folded into one 2020-2021 segment.

properties.line: SMART: Sonoma County Airport – San Rafael
properties.speed_source: computed from the April 2026 GTFS: Windsor - Larkspur (48.2 mi) scheduled at 81-84 min end to end. Applied to every era as an estimate; the 2017-2024 timetables were not checked.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap rail ways from cached Overpass degree tiles (mail.ru mirror; .osmcache in the site repo), routed by Dijkstra over all railway=rail ways with ways operated by 'Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit District' (Mainline Subdivision) costed 1x and everything else 3x, from the Windsor to the Larkspur GTFS stop. Earlier eras are the same trace clipped at the nearest trace node to the GTFS Sonoma County Airport and San Rafael stops.
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, 42.8 mi against the documented 43 mi (Wikipedia, first phase). All but ~0.1 mi lies on ways tagged operator=Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit District. No approximated legs. The agency GTFS shape was not used: it cuts corners by up to ~425 m on long straight-line legs. This is the alignment SMART rebuilt in 2010-2017 on the old Northwestern Pacific formation, which is its own era.

segments.note: Full revenue service began 25 Aug 2017 (preview runs Rohnert Park - Marin Civic Center from 29 Jun 2017 are not drawn as a separate span). The opening release promised 34 weekday trips and 10 on weekends. headway_min is an ESTIMATE: 17 trips each way spread over about 15 hours, not counted from a timetable. Service ended at San Rafael until the Larkspur extension opened 14 Dec 2019, so the last two weeks of 2019 really ran to Larkspur. No trains 28-29 Oct 2019 (PG&E power shutoffs).
sources: Segment-level: opening date and the Larkspur extension date from Wikipedia; 34 weekday / 10 weekend trips from SMART's own release announcing full service from 25 Aug 2017. Headway is derived, not counted.

All but ~0.1 mi lies on ways tagged operator=Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit District. No approximated legs. The agency GTFS shape was not used: it cuts corners by up to ~425 m on long straight-line legs. segments.note: Larkspur extension (with the new Novato Downtown station) opened 14 Dec 2019. From spring 2020 COVID-19 cut service to 8 weekday round trips with no weekend trains; May 2021 restored 13 weekday and 6 Saturday round trips. headway_min is an ESTIMATE averaged over the two years, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: Larkspur opening and the COVID reductions as stated on Wikipedia. Headway is derived from those round-trip counts, not from a timetable.

segments.note: Pre-pandemic schedules restored in 2022; Sunday service resumed 1 May 2022. Wikipedia gives 24 weekday and 12 weekend round trips before the Windsor opening. headway_min is an ESTIMATE assuming the same spread as the 2026 GTFS (also 24 weekday round trips); the 2022-2024 timetables were not checked.
sources: Segment-level: restoration dates and the 24-round-trip figure from Wikipedia. Headway assumed from the 2026 GTFS, not counted for these years.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, 48.2 mi against the documented 48 mi (Wikipedia, operational length). All but ~0.1 mi lies on ways tagged operator=Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit District. No approximated legs. The agency GTFS shape was not used: it cuts corners by up to ~425 m on long straight-line legs. This is the alignment SMART rebuilt in 2010-2017 on the old Northwestern Pacific formation, which is its own era.

segments.note: Windsor station opened 31 May 2025, extending service 3 mi north of Sonoma County Airport (Petaluma North is also open by the 2026 feed). April 2026 GTFS: 24 weekday trains each way, every 32 min at the peaks and 64 min midday; headway_min is the mean interval across the weekday span. Weekends run 12 each way. A Healdsburg extension broke ground in March 2026 (completion expected 2028) and is not drawn.
sources: Segment-level: Windsor opening date from Wikipedia; trip counts and headway counted from SMART's GTFS (feed of 14 Apr 2026, Schedule 16). 2025 headway assumed from the 2026 feed.
